sub_applications.name: Dilator Tip Forming
sub_applications.description: A tapered distal section engineered to expand tissue gradually and enable smooth advancement of sheath systems. Dilator tips require precise thermal forming to achieve a consistent taper, tight sheath-dilator fit, and atraumatic insertion.
sub_applications.long_description: Dilator tips are designed to create a smooth, controlled transition that allows clinicians to comfortably expand tissue and advance introducer sheaths without resistance or trauma. While the geometry appears straightforward, forming a reliable dilator taper requires exceptional control over heat, material flow, and internal support. Small deviations can result in rough edges, uneven tapering, or poor gap matching with the paired sheath—issues that directly impact insertion force, procedural efficiency, and physician satisfaction. With a wide range of tube diameters, wall structures, and polymer chemistries used across modern dilator systems, achieving consistent performance demands a highly repeatable forming process. ONEX meets this need through RF-driven temperature stability, engineered forming profiles, and a process-centric approach that produces smooth, concentric tapers with excellent sheath compatibility. The result is a dilator tip that advances cleanly, engages the sheath precisely, and delivers a dependable tactile experience in clinical use.

sub_applications.name: Sheath Tip Forming
sub_applications.description: A smooth, tapered distal tip engineered for easy vessel entry and reliable sheath–dilator pairing. Sheath tips require tight thermal control and precise geometry to ensure low-friction insertion and consistent clinical performance.
sub_applications.long_description: Sheath tips are critical components in introducer systems, functioning as the first structure that enters the vessel and guiding the sheath–dilator assembly during advancement. Their geometry—typically tapered, rounded, or a blend of both—directly affects insertion force, vessel trauma, and clinician confidence. Achieving a consistent, smooth tip is far more complex than simply heating the distal end. Variations in polymer stiffness, wall thickness, lubricity, and sheath–dilator gap requirements demand a finely tuned forming process that maintains uniformity while preventing deformation or surface defects. Undersized gaps cause binding; oversized gaps compromise stability. ONEX addresses these challenges with RF-based thermal precision, engineered die shaping, and a development-first approach that ensures every sheath tip meets exact dimensional, surface, and taper requirements. The result is a tip that enters smoothly, tracks predictably, and pairs tightly with its dilator—without gaps, drag, or unwanted friction.

sub_applications.name: Soft Tip
sub_applications.description: A soft, atraumatic distal tip thermally formed and bonded to the catheter shaft to enhance patient comfort and reduce tissue trauma. Soft tips require precise geometry and high-strength bonding to ensure reliable clinical performance.
sub_applications.long_description: Soft catheter tips are designed to provide a gentle, patient-friendly interface during insertion and navigation, making them essential in a wide range of diagnostic and interventional applications. These tips are typically formed from soft, flexible polymers—such as PU, PU blends, or PEBAX—and bonded to a stiffer catheter shaft to combine comfort with control. Achieving this balance requires exceptional precision: the tip must maintain a smooth profile, preserve internal lumen geometry, and form a strong, reliable bond to the shaft. Any variation in heat distribution, alignment, or material flow can lead to weak bonding, inconsistent softness, rough edges, or lumen deformation, all of which directly affect device safety and usability. With catheter designs varying widely in diameter, wall structure, and required softness levels, manufacturers need a process capable of forming and bonding tips with high repeatability. ONEX meets this challenge through RF-based thermal accuracy, precision-engineered dies, and controlled bonding methods that ensure a uniform transition from soft tip to shaft and maximum bond integrity. Whether used for soft tip bonding, soft-tip guidewire assemblies, or fully formed soft distal segments, ONEX systems deliver consistent, high-quality results.

ONEX delivers this level of precision through RF-driven heating profiles, engineered micro-scale forming dies, and process strategies designed specifically for metal–polymer composite structures. The result is a repeatable, high-quality guidewire tip that maintains coating integrity, preserves core alignment, and provides the tactile feedback clinicians rely on during demanding interventions.

sub_applications.name: Tracheal Tip
sub_applications.description: A precisely formed angled or radiused distal tip designed for tracheal access and airway procedures. Tracheal tips require accurate thermal forming to maintain smooth surfaces, controlled angles, and consistent lumen geometry.
sub_applications.long_description: Tracheal catheter tips are specialized angle-tip geometries engineered to guide the tube smoothly into the airway while minimizing tissue trauma. These tips may incorporate a defined bevel, an angled cut, or a radiused straight end—each requiring high precision to achieve reliable insertion characteristics. Because tracheal access involves delicate tissue and curved anatomical pathways, the tip must deliver a balance of directional control, smooth surface finish, and predictable stiffness. Achieving this consistently is challenging: variations in PVC durometer, wall thickness, and tip-angle geometry can easily produce sharp edges, asymmetry, or lumen distortion if thermal forming is not tightly controlled. ONEX ensures this precision through RF-driven thermal accuracy, engineered angle-forming dies, and a repeatable forming process that preserves lumen integrity while producing clean, smooth, clinically safe tip geometries. The result is a tracheal tip that advances comfortably, follows anatomical curves with minimal resistance, and provides clinicians with dependable performance across diverse airway procedures.

sub_applications.name: PEEK Tube Forming
sub_applications.description: A high-performance tip-forming application designed for PEEK tubing—one of the most demanding materials in medical manufacturing. PEEK tips require extreme thermal precision, tight dimensional control, and repeatable forming to achieve reliable, defect-free geometries.
sub_applications.long_description: PEEK catheter tips represent one of the most technically challenging thermoforming applications due to the material’s exceptionally high melting point, low fluidity, and strict biocompatibility requirements. PEEK must be processed at elevated temperatures while maintaining dimensional stability, wall uniformity, and mechanical strength. Even slight deviations in heating, cooling rate, or pressure control can lead to incomplete forming, uneven crystallization, internal voids, or brittle regions that compromise device safety. As PEEK tubing is widely used in advanced cardiovascular, neurological, urological, and implantable applications, manufacturers must achieve flawless tip geometry and surface finish to meet clinical performance expectations. ONEX delivers the precision required through RF-driven thermal accuracy, advanced temperature control strategies, and tooling engineered to support difficult-to-flow polymers like PEEK. Our process development ensures reliable shaping of mushroom tips, closed ends, tapered profiles, radius tips, and other high-performance geometries while preserving strength, chemical resistance, and biocompatibility—allowing manufacturers to confidently scale production in even the most demanding applications.

sub_applications.name: Flared Conical Shape
sub_applications.description: A precision-formed flared end designed to create a larger, reinforced opening for component interfaces, connectors, and fluid pathways. Flares require controlled thermal expansion and exact geometric shaping to ensure reliable fitment, sealing, and mechanical strength.
sub_applications.long_description: Flared catheter ends are used across a wide range of medical devices to create enlarged openings that support fluid transfer, secure interconnections, prevent pullout, or interface with downstream assemblies. These flares must be formed with exceptional dimensional accuracy to ensure smooth transitions, strong mechanical engagement, and consistent flow characteristics. Because tubing materials, wall thicknesses, and flare geometries can vary dramatically—from simple straight enlargements to curved funnel profiles or stepped flares—the forming process must tightly manage heat, material expansion, and die alignment. Soft or low-durometer polymers may thin excessively if overheated, while high-performance materials like PTFE or PEEK require aggressive temperature control to prevent cracking or incomplete forming. ONEX RF systems address these challenges through uniform heating, force-controlled expansion, and precision-engineered flaring dies that deliver repeatable, symmetric flares across a broad polymer and size range. This ensures dependable sealing, enhanced flow dynamics, and strong mechanical engagement for both simple and advanced medical assemblies.

sub_applications.name: Flange Tip
sub_applications.description: A mechanically reinforced distal or proximal enlargement designed to anchor catheter components, prevent pullout, and interface securely with interlocking hardware. Flanged ends require precise geometric forming to ensure consistent fitment and long-term mechanical reliability.
sub_applications.long_description: Flanged catheter ends are engineered to create a secure mechanical interface between the tube and another component—whether that’s a connector, hub, valve, introducer system, or retention fixture. Unlike flares, which primarily widen an opening, flanges create a defined, right-angle or ring-shaped structure that provides anti-pullout strength, positional stability, and a repeatable engagement geometry. Because these features must withstand mechanical loading, repeated connection cycles, and sometimes elevated pressures, flange dimensions must be formed with exceptional accuracy. Variations in OD growth, thickness, flange height, or internal transitions can compromise fitment or lead to premature mechanical failure. The challenge intensifies when working across a broad range of tubing sizes, wall thicknesses, and polymer types—from flexible PU to rigid PEEK. ONEX RF systems provide the precise, repeatable heat control and forming stability needed to create consistent flange geometry, ensuring durable mechanical performance and compatibility with interlocking components across diverse catheter applications.

sub_applications.description: A rounded, enlarged distal end designed to provide reliable anchoring, secure positioning, and controlled retention within anatomical cavities or interlocking device components. Mushroom tips require precise thermal forming to achieve smooth contours, consistent expansion, and strong mechanical performance.

The expanded, rounded profile helps anchor the device within an anatomical space—such as an abscess cavity—or within an interlocking component in a multi-part catheter system. These tips must be formed with smooth, controlled contours to prevent tissue irritation and ensure consistent drainage or device function. Achieving a uniform mushroom profile requires exceptional precision: uneven heating or material flow can lead to asymmetry, thin spots, or sharp edges that compromise both mechanical engagement and patient comfort. Because mushroom tips are manufactured in a wide range of diameters, wall structures, and polymer types—from soft PU blends to stiffer thermoplastics—consistent forming depends on tightly controlled RF heating and well-designed tooling. ONEX systems deliver this repeatability through precision die engineering, uniform thermal control, and process development focused on producing stable, symmetric, and reliable mushroom geometries for both drainage and retention applications.

sub_applications.name: Soft Tip
sub_applications.description: A soft, atraumatic distal tip thermally formed and bonded to the catheter shaft to enhance patient comfort and reduce tissue trauma. Soft tips require precise geometry and high-strength bonding to ensure reliable clinical performance.
sub_applications.long_description: Soft catheter tips are designed to provide a gentle, patient-friendly interface during insertion and navigation, making them essential in a wide range of diagnostic and interventional applications. These tips are typically formed from soft, flexible polymers—such as PU, PU blends, or PEBAX—and bonded to a stiffer catheter shaft to combine comfort with control. Achieving this balance requires exceptional precision: the tip must maintain a smooth profile, preserve internal lumen geometry, and form a strong, reliable bond to the shaft. Any variation in heat distribution, alignment, or material flow can lead to weak bonding, inconsistent softness, rough edges, or lumen deformation, all of which directly affect device safety and usability. With catheter designs varying widely in diameter, wall structure, and required softness levels, manufacturers need a process capable of forming and bonding tips with high repeatability. ONEX meets this challenge through RF-based thermal accuracy, precision-engineered dies, and controlled bonding methods that ensure a uniform transition from soft tip to shaft and maximum bond integrity. Whether used for soft tip bonding, soft-tip guidewire assemblies, or fully formed soft distal segments, ONEX systems deliver consistent, high-quality results.

sub_applications.name: Butt Welding
sub_applications.description: A precise thermal joining method used to fuse two catheter tube segments into a single, continuous structure. Butt welds create high-strength, leak-resistant joints essential for multi-segment shafts, soft–to–rigid transitions, and balloon or braided integrations.
sub_applications.long_description: Butt welding is a foundational process in advanced catheter manufacturing, enabling two tube segments—often with different materials, durometers, or structural properties—to be fused into a continuous, high-performance shaft. This technique is critical for multi-segment catheter designs used in vascular, urinary, gastrointestinal, and respiratory applications, where each tube segment must contribute a specific mechanical or functional characteristic. Unlike adhesive bonding, butt welds produce a sterile, high-strength connection without introducing foreign materials, reducing contamination risks and improving long-term durability. Achieving a clean, reliable weld requires precise control over heat, axial pressure, alignment, and material flow. Even slight deviations can lead to lumen deformation, weak joints, surface roughness, or internal flow disturbances. With a broad range of tubing sizes, polymer chemistries, and welded segment geometries, manufacturers need a forming system capable of delivering uniform, repeatable weld quality. ONEX RF welding platforms provide the accuracy needed to form smooth transitions, maintain lumen integrity, and produce consistent mechanical performance—whether welding soft tips to shafts, balloon segments to catheter bodies, or braided to non-braided sections.

sub_applications.name: Overlap Welding
sub_applications.description: A high-strength joining method where one tube segment overlaps another, creating an extended melt interface for superior bonding and structural durability. Overlap welds are essential for multi-segment catheters, balloon-to-shaft assemblies, and applications requiring smooth, reinforced transitions.
sub_applications.long_description: Overlap welding is a critical technique in catheter manufacturing, used to fuse one tube segment onto another by creating an extended, overlapping melt interface. This configuration increases bond strength, improves load distribution, and delivers a smoother, more gradual transition compared to a standard butt weld. Overlap welds are especially important in balloon catheter assemblies, where thin film balloons must be securely joined to the catheter shaft without creating stress concentrations, rough edges, or irregularities that could impair inflation performance or damage vessel walls. Because the process involves melting two layers of material simultaneously while preserving lumen integrity and surface smoothness, it demands extremely precise thermal control and alignment. Variations in overlap length, tubing stiffness, or polymer melt behavior can significantly affect weld quality. ONEX RF-based welding systems address these challenges through uniform heating, optimized forming geometry, and process repeatability that ensures strong, clean, and reliable overlap joints across a wide range of catheter designs and materials.

sub_applications.name: Angiographic Tip
sub_applications.description: A smooth, rounded distal tip designed for atraumatic vessel entry and precise contrast delivery. Angiographic tips require accurate thermal forming and strong, reliable bonding to the catheter shaft to ensure consistent clinical performance.
sub_applications.long_description: Angiographic catheter tips must combine a smooth, radius-shaped geometry with a strong thermal bond to the main catheter shaft to ensure safe vessel entry and reliable contrast injection. These tips must maintain a precise profile that minimizes trauma during navigation while preserving lumen integrity for consistent flow rates and injection pressures. Because angiographic catheters vary widely in diameter, polymer blends, stiffness, and durometer, creating a dependable angiographic tip requires a forming process that can precisely manage heat, alignment, and bond strength. Inconsistent thermal distribution or suboptimal alignment during bonding can weaken the interface, distort the radius, or create uneven surfaces that compromise catheter tracking. ONEX delivers the repeatability and precision required through RF-driven thermal control, engineered forming dies, and bond integration methods that ensure uniform radius geometry, smooth transitions, and maximum-strength bonding for high-performance angiographic systems.
